## Funding

I have substantively contributed to and/or taken a relevant role in the grant applications of the following scientific projects.

### Competitive grants

#### External (national / international)

##### As CI

**[Language Data Commons of Australia HASS RDC (LDaCA-RDC)](https://www.ldaca.edu.au/)**
Scheme: Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences (HASS) Research Data Commons (RDC) and Indigenous Research Capability Program
Funding body: Australian Research Data Commons (ARDC)
Role: Advisory committee & CI
Project lead: Michael Haugh (UQ)
Collaborators: Various Australian & international stakeholders (researchers and institutions, e.g. universities, First Languages Australia)
Funding period: 2021–2029 (phase I: 2021–2023, phase II: 2024–2029)

In Australia, large language data collections exist, some housed in well-established archives (such as Trove), but many stored in short-lived repositories. LDaCA aims to consolidate these efforts into a nationally integrated research infrastructure. It aims to: (1) establish a governance board representing key stakeholders, (2) develop a comprehensive policy framework for access to language data, (3) create a shared technical infrastructure across institutions, (4) develop a portal for the discovery and access to language data, and (5) engage researchers and communities to secure and make accessible Australia's linguistic heritage.

**[Australian Text Analytics Platform (ATAP)](https://www.atap.edu.au/)**
Scheme: Platforms Program
Funding body: [Australian Research Data Commons (ARDC)](https://ardc.edu.au/)
Role: Steering committee, CI, & Chair of the User Advisory Group
Project lead: Michael Haugh (UQ)
Collaborators: Various Australian & international stakeholders
Funding period: 2021–2023 (integrated into LDaCA as of 2024)

Text analysis in Australian research is conducted either at a basic, generic level or at a highly specialized level with custom code. ATAP aimed to fill the gap between these two approaches, developing an integrated, notebook-based platform for processing and extracting text data.

##### As Partner Investigator / Collaborator

**Interfaces to Data for Historical Social Network Analysis and Research (SoNAR (IDH))**
Funding body: Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG)
Role: International Collaborator
Project lead: Gerhard Müller
Collaborators: Various German libraries and universities & international stakeholders

SoNAR (IDH), Interfaces to Data for Historical Social Network Analysis and Research, examines and evaluates approaches to build and operate an advanced research technology environment supporting Historical Network Analysis and related research. Project partners from various fields — historiography, information visualization, artificial intelligence and computer sciences, and information science — work on this topic from their respective perspective.

#### Internal (UQ and institutional schemes)

##### As Lead CI

**Statistics for Linguists: A Practical Introduction Using R**
Scheme: Open Textbooks @ UQ grant
Funding body: University of Queensland Library
Role: Project lead
Year: 2026/27

**ClimDis@UZH: Finalising a UQ–UEF–UZH EU Horizon Application on Climate Change Discourse**
Scheme: Global Partnerships 2026
Funding body: University of Queensland
Role: Lead
Collaborators: International academics
Year: 2026

Public understanding of climate change is shaped not only by scientific evidence but by a complex, multilingual digital information landscape in which social media, political rhetoric, and official reports compete for authority and reach. ClimDis is a trilateral computational corpus study of climate change discourse in English, German, and Finnish, developed in partnership between the University of Queensland (UQ), the University of Eastern Finland (UEF), and the University of Zurich (UZH, a formal UQ Strategic Partner since 2021).

**From banter to abuse: pragmatics-informed detection of hate speech for democratic resilience**
Scheme: UQ Horizon Europe Seed and Engagement Fund
Funding body: University of Queensland
Role: Project lead & CI
Collaborators: Michael Haugh (UQ), Mikko Laitinen (UEF), Gerold Schneider (UZH)
Year: 2026

**Fucking Twitter: a contrastive network and text analytic approach to curse word use in the Australian, British, and US American Twitterspheres**
Scheme: [Digital Cultures and Societies Hub](https://hass.uq.edu.au/centre-digital-cultures-societies)
Funding body: University of Queensland
Role: Project lead
Collaborators: Marissa Takahashi (QUT / Australian Digital Observatory), Mikko Laitinen (UEF), Paula Rautionaho (UEF), Michael Haugh (UQ), Sam Hames (UQ)
Duration: 8/2022 – 7/2023

This project empirically assesses the assumption that Australians swear frequently by comparing Twitter data from Australia, the UK, and the US. It develops a prototype using computational methods to clean Twitter data, detect and extract swear words, and analyze their frequency and usage contexts.

**[VowelChartProject](https://www.zlh-hamburg.de/entwicklungsvorhaben/lehrlabore/l3prof-lehrlabor-lehrerprofessionalisierung.html)**
Scheme: [L3Prof](https://www.zlh-hamburg.de/entwicklungsvorhaben/lehrlabore/l3prof-lehrlabor-lehrerprofessionalisierung.html), Universität Hamburg
Funding body: Bundesministerium für Bildung und Forschung (BMBF), via L3Prof
Role: Project lead & Principal Investigator (PI)
Duration: 9/2016 – 9/2018

The VowelChartProject extracted vowel formants from German, Russian, and Spanish learners of English using PRAAT and R to investigate where, why, and to what extent English learners differ from native English speakers in vowel production and word-final devoicing. Students received personalized vowel charts and written feedback after participating.

##### As Partner Investigator / Collaborator

**LLMs4HASS: Exploring the Use of Large Language Models for Qualitative and Interpretive Research in the Humanities and Social Sciences**
Scheme: [Centre for Digital Cultures & Societies](https://hass.uq.edu.au/centre-digital-cultures-societies) — 2026 Funding Scheme
Funding body: University of Queensland
Role: Researcher
Project lead: Michael Haugh (UQ)
Collaborators: Laurence Anthony (Waseda)
Year: 2026

LLMs4HASS investigates how large language models can support qualitative HASS research, while addressing analytical limitations, privacy concerns, and heterogeneous data formats through practical, open-source tools for harmonised, analysis-ready research workflows.

**Studying the Development and Contestation of Discourses and Ideologies through Computational Approaches to Big Data on Online Platforms**

Funding body: University of Queensland
Role: Collaborator
Project lead: Sam Hames (UQ)
Collaborators: Michael Haugh (UQ)
Year: 2023
